The Sabbath question is not a minor denominational disagreement. It sits at the intersection of authority, prophecy, and loyalty — whose word we trust, whose law we follow, and where our ultimate allegiance lies. Why study this carefully?
God commands it — The fourth commandment is the only commandment God prefaced with the word "Remember" (Exodus 20:8). He knew we would forget.
Prophecy predicted it — Daniel 7:25 foretold that an earthly power would "think to change times and law." The change of the Sabbath is the most visible fulfillment of this prophecy.

Before examining the neuroscience, we must address the most common biblical misunderstanding: Did Jesus make alcoholic wine? Did God endorse drinking alcohol? The answer: No. The Bible uses the word "wine" for two completely different substances:
Yayin (יַיִן) - Generic term for "wine" (can mean fermented or unfermented)
Tirosh (תִּירוֹשׁ) - "New wine" / fresh grape juice (always unfermented)
Oinos (οἶνος) - Generic term for "wine" (can mean fermented or unfermented)

Gleukos (γλεῦκος) - "New wine" / sweet wine (unfermented grape juice) Context determines meaning. When the Bible blesses wine, it means fresh grape juice. When it condemns wine, it means fermented alcohol.
